rawFindings.title: Incorrect logic for detecting multiline node in comma-dangle rule
rawFindings.explanation: The variable 'lastTokenOnNewLine' was replaced with 'nodeIsMultiLine' to detect if the node is multiline based on the node's start and end lines instead of the penultimate token's location. This change corrects the condition to check whether the node spans multiple lines instead of relying on token end line positions, aligning better with the 'always-multiline' option logic.
rawFindings.suggestion: This change is correct and aligns with expected behavior. No fix needed.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect multi-line check for dangling commas in 'always-multiline' option
rawFindings.explanation: The original code checks if the dangling comma is on a new line by comparing node.loc.end.line with penultimateToken.loc.end.line. The fix replaces this with a flag nodeIsMultiLine indicating whether the entire node spans multiple lines, which more directly matches the intent of the 'always-multiline' option. Using nodeIsMultiLine prevents false negatives or positives when node tokens are on the same line but the node actually spans multiple lines, ensuring correct error reporting.
rawFindings.suggestion: Use a node-level multiline flag (nodeIsMultiLine) instead of comparing penultimateToken location for checking if dangling commas are valid under 'always-multiline'. Replace lastTokenOnNewLine assignment at line 28 with nodeIsMultiLine = node.loc.start.line !== node.loc.end.line and then use this flag in the conditional checks.
